text:
Cole Smith is in Chicago for the parts of hockey that don't show up on a scoresheet. In 23 games he has 53 hits, two goals and five points while playing about 14 minutes a night, and the Blackhawks lean on him as a big, fast body (his top skating speed sits in the 93rd percentile) who can kill a penalty. He missed a practice with an injury on Nov. 16, then played the next night.

The honest read on his offense is that there isn't much of it. His own chances are thin (3.21 expected goals, meaning the quality of shots he has taken), and at five on five the Blackhawks get only about 42% of the expected goals when he is out there. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his game isn't built on creating at even strength.

There is one bit of bad luck worth knowing about: Chicago has scored 6.3 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. That tends to even out, so a few more points should drift his way. Just don't mistake that for a scoring role.
